core_conclusion: TranscriptFormer is a family of generative single-cell foundation models trained on up to 112 million cells from 12 species spanning 1.53 billion years of evolution. It achieves state-of-the-art cell-type classification even across >685 million years of divergence and zero-shot disease-state identification in human cells, and developmental trajectories, phylogenetic relationships and cellular hierarchies emerge in its representations without explicit supervision.
why_it_matters: Makes cross-species comparison of transcriptional programs a computable operation rather than a curatorial one; demonstrates extreme out-of-distribution generalization across evolutionary distance; delivers zero-shot clinical signal in annotation-scarce settings; and shows biological organizing structure emerging unsupervised, so the embedding itself becomes a hypothesis-generation instrument.
why_nature: Editorial fit for Science: a universal claim about cellular organization across the tree of life rather than a single-system result; evolution used as the axis of evidence, giving reach into evolutionary biology, genomics and machine learning simultaneously; unsupervised emergence of development and phylogeny as a genuinely surprising scientific finding; an immediate translational hook via zero-shot disease-state identification; and a platform-type contribution (a model family plus a cross-species atlas) that functions as community infrastructure.
